newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude prices down, but premium slide stops.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude prices down, but premium slide stops.

text.p: Asian crude prices were lower in outright terms on Thursday, but the slide in Middle East premiums appeared to flatten out, traders said.
Oman traded between MPM +8 and MPM +9.5 cents for full cargoes, traders said. A European trader sold 150,000 barrels of Oman crude at MPM +11 cents, the highest premium in the past two days.
Murban held at ADNOC +17 and +18 cents, traders said, reflected in two deals, one between a South Korean refiner and a U.S. major and the second between a European major and a Japanese trader.
Traders said the support for prices had come through the absence of aggressive selling of term barrels into the market.
Further support could come from talk that South Korean refineries were considering run cuts. The major refineries in South Korea denied such plans.
Industry sources said they would expect the refineries to cut production together because of their drive to maintain market share.
One South Korean source said if only a handful of refiners cut production, the shortfall would be swiftly filled by the other refiners.

Traders were waiting on the result of the Bangchak tender for the next price indication. Industry sources said a handful of Oman cargoes had been offered into the tender, with some offering single digit premiums.
They said one Tapis cargo, a Belida and some Australian grades had also been offered.
A major was offering early February Tapis at a premium of $1.20, well below last deal done at $1.75 and reflective of the crashing price of products.
